author: Craig Sesker
title: Express continue to roll with another win at Carson Park - NewsBreak
text:
By Craig Sesker ,
1 hours ago
The Eau Claire Express continue to stockpile momentum. And victories.
The Express kept rolling toward the Northwoods League baseball playoffs with another impressive performance Wednesday night.
Eau Claire's latest win featured a familiar formula of excellent pitching, timely hitting and superb defense.
The first place Express looked sharp before a big crowd, downing Duluth 5-1 in front of 1,538 fans at Carson Park.
Eau Claire improved to 25-8 in the second half.
"These guys just continue to be really consistent," Express manager Dale Varsho said. "Our pitching staff was really good again and we had some guys come up with some clutch hits."
Eau Claire starter Mike Erspamer was fabulous in 2 2/3 dominant innings. He struck out five while allowing one hit and no runs.
Erspamer was on a pitch limit Wednesday to preserve his arm for the postseason. He threw 33 pitches, including 22 for strikes.
"The plan was for Erspamer to throw 30 pitches," Varsho said. "He is going to go for us in Game 1. I want to make sure he is ready for Sunday.
"He has some great stuff. He's probably one of the best pitchers we've had in a long time, especially with his fastball and unbelievable breaking ball. He's fun to watch."
Reliever Jackson Niederweder (5-1) earned the victory. He struck out four batters in 3 1/3 innings.
Sam Malone followed with two innings of shutout relief before Brock Adamson pitched a scoreless ninth for the winning team.
The offense relied on three solo homers, from Hollon Brock, Jaxon Schumacher and Adam Salazar, to prevail on Wednesday.
"Those home runs were big," Varsho said. "All those guys came through."
Brock blasted a long ball to left field in the second inning to give his team a 1-0 lead.
Schumacher crushed a no-doubter to left field in the seventh inning. He flipped his bat after drilling a ball that sailed high over the outfield fence.
"I was just trying to hit the ball hard somewhere," he said. "I swung through a fastball and then he threw me something slower. He hung a changeup and I was able to get a hold of it."
The left-handed batting Salazar followed by launching his home run to right field.
"I caught a curveball," he said. "I was looking for that pitch in that count and I got it."
Eau Claire continues to battle La Crosse for home field advantage in the first round of the playoffs.
The Express trail the Loggers by one game for best overall record in their division with three regular season games remaining.
"We want to have home field advantage," Salazar said. "We are playing well. Our whole lineup, one through nine, we just play good team baseball. We are really looking forward to the playoffs. It's exciting."
No matter what happens in the next three games, Eau Claire is peaking at the right time.
"It's awesome to be in the playoffs," Schumacher said. "It doesn't matter where you are playing, it's just exciting to have the opportunity to keep the season going. We can't wait."
